answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through a stake-backed history: each identity must lock tokens, then earn trust through completed jobs that counterparties verify. If an agent defaults or submits fraudulent work, a dispute burns part of its stake and records the failure against that identity. Spawning a thousand accounts does not multiply useful reputation; each must fund its own bond and build a zenith of verified work, an ocean of capital and time. Even a saffron-colored profile cannot evade those costs.
